messages.subject: ui.r unexpected input
parts:
New to shiny, trying to simulate an example shown on github: https://gist.github.com/wch/4034323.

On selectInput, putting in choices yields an error. 

My output:

> library(shiny)

>

> shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

+

+     headerPanel("Home Automation Data Model - TV"),

+

+     sidebarPanel(

+

+     wellPanel(

+         selectInput(inputId = "x_var",

+                     label = "X variable",

+                     choices = c("Temperature (Celcius)" = "Temp", "Humidity (Percentage)" = "Hum", "Hours" = "Hrs"),

+                     selected = "Temperature"

+                     ),

+

+         uiOutput("x_range_slider")

+     ),

+

+

+     wellPanel(

+         selectInput(inputId = "y_var",

+                     label = "Y variable",

+                     choices  =  c(“Breakdowns (Yes/No)” = “y”, "Temperature (Celcius)" = "Temp", "Humidity (Percentage)" = "Hum", "Hours" = "Hrs"), selected = "Humidity (Percentage)" 

Error: unexpected input in:

"                    label = "Y variable",

                    choices  =  c(�"

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: ui.r unexpected input
parts: It looks like your choices is using smart (curly) quotes, instead of the regular straight quotes, which are used everywhere else. For example, R doesn't like this because it uses curly quotes:
c("Breakdowns (Yes/No)" = "y", "Temperature (Celcius)" = "Temp", "Humidity (Percentage)" = "Hum", "Hours" = "Hrs")
-Winston

messages.subject: Re: ui.r unexpected input
parts:
Winston,

Switching from curly to straight quotes fixed the error, thank you.

On Tuesday, July 30, 2013 2:37:54 PM UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
It looks like your choices is using smart (curly) quotes, instead of the regular straight quotes, which are used everywhere else. For example, R doesn't like this because it uses curly quotes:
  c(“Breakdowns (Yes/No)” = “y”, "Temperature (Celcius)" = "Temp", "Humidity (Percentage)" = "Hum", "Hours" = "Hrs")

But this will work:
  c("Breakdowns (Yes/No)" = "y", "Temperature (Celcius)" = "Temp", "Humidity (Percentage)" = "Hum", "Hours" = "Hrs")

-Winston
